title: Anti-exfil signing for BIP340 and ECDSA: test vectors
encoding: All byte strings are lowercase hex. An empty message is the empty string.
derivation: sk = SHA256(seed || "/sk"), rho = SHA256(seed || "/rho"), a 32-byte m = SHA256(seed || "/m"), and the long message is SHA256(seed || "/m/j") for j = 0..31 concatenated. seed is the ASCII string in each valid case.

classes.valid: sk, m, rho -> pk, hc, R0_bytes, sig. A device must produce these bytes; a host must accept the tuple.
classes.reject: A host must reject the (pk, m, rho, R0_bytes, sig) tuple. No secret key is given.
classes.forced_hash: Needs a hash override. forced_hash.tag output is replaced by the stated 32 bytes; every other hash is computed normally.

reject.isolates: BIP340 Verify: pk must be the x coordinate of a curve point
reject.comment: pk is an x with no curve point. R0 is valid and the signature is (x(W), s) with s*G = W, which satisfies the verification equation when the pk term is dropped, so only the failed lift of pk refuses it.

R0_bytes begins with 0x04 (an uncompressed prefix). The signature is an ordinary valid signature from the key whose nonce is t = H(R0_bytes || rho), so x(W) = x(t*G) would match if R0 were dropped. Only the failed parse of R0_bytes refuses it.

R0_bytes is 0x02 followed by an x with no curve point. The signature is an ordinary valid signature from the key whose nonce is t = H(R0_bytes || rho), so x(W) = x(t*G) would match if R0 were dropped. Only the failed parse of R0_bytes refuses it.

forced_hash.comment: The nonce hash returns 0, so k0 = 0 and the device must fail.
The nonce hash returns n, which reduces to 0 mod n, so the device must fail.
The point-tweak hash returns n, so t >= n and the device must fail in step 4.
The point-tweak hash returns 2^256-1, so t >= n and the device must fail in step 4.
The point-tweak hash returns n - k0, where k0 is this vector's base nonce, so k' = 0 and the device must fail in step 4.

forced_hash.why: t = n - k0, so k' = (k0 + t) mod n = 0

forced_hash.comment: The host's point-tweak hash returns n, so t >= n and the host must reject the otherwise valid tuple.
The host's point-tweak hash returns 2^256-1, so t >= n and the host must reject.
The host's point-tweak hash returns n - k0, so W = R0 + t*G is the point at infinity and the host must reject.

forced_hash.why: t = n - k0, so W = infinity

forced_hash.isolates: W = R0 + t*G with R0 = t*G must be computed as a doubling
forced_hash.comment: The point-tweak hash returns 5 and R0 = 5*G, so W = R0 + t*G = 10*G is the doubling case of the point addition. The signature is valid with nonce 10, so the host must accept. A host that fails on R0 = t*G refuses it.

forced_hash.isolates: W = R0 + t*G must not be the point at infinity
forced_hash.comment: The point-tweak hash returns 5 and R0 = -5*G, so W = R0 + t*G is the point at infinity. The signature is valid with nonce n - 10 and would pass every later check if W were computed as the double of R0, so only the infinity check refuses it.

forced_hash.isolates: BIP340 Verify: s must be below n
forced_hash.comment: The point-tweak hash returns 0 and the BIP340 challenge hash returns 5. R0 = -5*P, sig = (x(R0), n). Reduced mod n the s half is 0, which would satisfy R = s*G - e*P, so only the range check s < n refuses it.
